title: What kind of business fits you?
intro: Not which idea. Which shape. Twenty businesses on this site, sorted into six kinds, and this points at the kind before you argue about the idea.
og_line: Eight questions, six kinds of business, and the twenty real ones behind them.

cta.title: See all twenty
cta.label: Compare all twenty
cta.blurb: Every one of the twenty compared on what it costs to start, what the margin looks like, whether demand is growing and what ends most of them.

questions.q: Saturday morning, nothing booked. What sounds least like a chore?

options.a: Fixing something that has been annoying you
Cooking for more people than strictly necessary
Explaining something to someone who asked
Rearranging a shelf until it photographs well

questions.q: Which of these would you actually enjoy owning?

options.a: A shop that takes orders overnight
A place people have to be certified to run
A van with your name on it
A counter with a queue at it

questions.q: A stranger asks what you do. The version you would be proud to say:

options.a: I sort out the thing they were dreading
I make the thing they put on their wall
I ship about forty of these a week
I run a licensed practice

questions.q: What would you rather be judged on?

options.a: Whether it works now that I have left
Whether they came back next week
Whether the advice turned out to be right
Whether it looks the way they hoped
Enough for stock, then more for ads
Real money and a wait for approval
A few thousand for kit and a vehicle
Enough for a room, a fit out and an inspection

questions.q: The part that would bore you into quitting:

options.a: Doing the same job for the same person forever
Work nobody ever looks at twice
Talking to customers all day
Trading before the paperwork is done
Wherever the job is
A kitchen, early
Anywhere with signal
A place people come to, that had to be signed off

questions.q: Which sentence do you want to be true in a year?

options.a: People ask for me by name
It ran for a week without me
Three of us are on the road
People queue

results.name: Work you do with your hands
results.headline: A van, a skill and a route.
results.body: A van, a skill and a route. The cheapest of these to start, which is exactly why somebody else can start one next week.
results.cost: Nobody needs you specifically. You compete on showing up and on price.

results.name: Work people can taste
results.headline: The one everybody romanticises.
results.body: The one everybody romanticises, and the one with the thinnest margins. Perishable stock, daily labour and a health inspector.
results.cost: The hours. Food does not wait, so the business sets your day rather than the other way round.

results.name: Selling what you already know
results.headline: Somebody already asks you about this at parties.
results.body: Somebody already asks you about this at parties. The startup cost is close to nothing and the hard part is that nobody knows you do it.
results.cost: It stops earning the moment you stop working. Every week spent selling is a week not billed.

results.name: Selling an actual thing
results.headline: A shop that is open while you sleep.
results.body: Inventory, postage and a shop that is open while you sleep. The only one here that can earn without you present.
results.cost: Customer acquisition. The shop is open, and empty, until you pay to fill it.

results.name: Work people hire you for by eye
results.headline: They pick you because of how it looks.
results.body: They pick you because of how it looks, which means the portfolio is the business and the pricing conversation never gets easier.
results.cost: Being judged on taste. The work is personal, so the rejection is too.

links.label: How to start social media agency

results.name: Work that sits behind a licence
results.headline: Higher walls, fewer neighbours.
results.body: Higher walls and fewer neighbours. Somebody has to sign off before you can trade, which is exactly why there is less competition once you are in.
results.cost: The paperwork arrives before the first customer does, and it never fully stops.
